overview.text: eTranzact announced director changes on October 13, 2026, after 5.17 billion ordinary shares (56.18%) transferred to Trademarks Global Concepts Limited. Xenergi acquired about 49.6% of Premier Paints.
INEC removed 1.6 million names from the voters' register, according to Premium Times.
NERC approved N30 billion as the third tranche of the Meter Acquisition Fund, allocated among eleven DisCos in proportion to their contributions. Installations must finish by 31 May 2027.
The House of Representatives urged NNPC Ltd to translate Petroleum Industry Act 2021 reforms into increased oil production and investment, at a retreat in Abuja on Monday.
Raenest acquired 100% ownership of Remitise, a UK-based payments company registered with the FCA.

cards.headline: eTranzact, MTN Nigeria, lead boardroom shake-ups as 9M 2026 earnings roll in
cards.what_happened: A wave of board changes accompanied NGX-listed companies' nine-month 2026 results, led by eTranzact International Plc replacing five directors after 56.18% of its shares passed to Trademarks Global Concepts Limited.
key_facts: eTranzact announced director changes on October 13, 2026, after 5.17 billion ordinary shares (56.18%) transferred to Trademarks Global Concepts Limited.
Xenergi acquired approximately 49.6% of Premier Paints' issued share capital.
cards.ownership_caveat: Ownership details as reported by Nairametrics; not verified with CAC records.

cards.headline: ICPC amends charges against fake PFIPC DG
cards.what_happened: The ICPC has amended its charges against Adeniyi Adeyemi, the purported Director-General of the non-existent Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council, increasing the counts from 22 to 36 and adding four defendants. The FCT High Court in Maitama adjourned the case to November 18 for arraignment of all defendants after a defendant was reported hospitalised.
key_facts: ICPC amended charges against Adeniyi Adeyemi, increasing counts from 22 to 36 and adding four defendants.
Adeyemi allegedly sought over N27bn as a take-off grant and another N3.8bn for personnel costs by forging official documents.
analysis: As reported by Punch; AURA has not checked court or agency records. An allegation or charge is not a finding of guilt.
named: Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission

cards.headline: BREAKING: NERC approves N30 billion to provide free meters to Band A, Band B customers
cards.what_happened: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved N30 billion for the third tranche of the Meter Acquisition Fund (MAF) to provide free electricity meters to unmetered Band A customers and accelerate metering for Band B customers. Under Order No. NERC/2026/121, the tranche takes effect from November 2, 2026, with all installations to be completed by May 31, 2027.
key_facts: Funds will be distributed among the 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos) according to their contributions to the Fund.
analysis: Why it matters: The programme commits N30 billion of public-linked funds to meter procurement across 11 DisCos, with contracts required to be filed with NERC, which strengthens oversight of how the money is spent.
Court outcome as reported by Nairametrics; AURA has not checked court records.

cards.headline: INEC removes 1.6 million names from voters’ register, fingers 54 officials
cards.what_happened: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has removed 1.6 million names from the voters' register. The electoral body has also named 54 officials in connection with the exercise.
key_facts: INEC removed 1.6 million names from the voters' register.
analysis: Why it matters: The removals and the naming of officials bear on the accuracy of Nigeria's voters' register and on accountability within the electoral agency.

cards.headline: DisCos get N30bn as NERC disburse third tranch of meter acquisition fund
cards.what_happened: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved N30 billion as the third tranche of the Meter Acquisition Fund, to be allocated among eleven Distribution Companies (DisCos) in proportion to their contributions. Under Order No. NERC/2026/121, DisCos must run transparent procurement involving eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers and Meter Asset Providers, with installations due by 31 May 2027.
key_facts: NERC approved N30 billion as the third tranche of the Meter Acquisition Fund.
The fund is allocated among eleven DisCos in proportion to their contributions to the Fund.
Payment to selected providers is made 70 percent on verified delivery and 30 percent on complete installation.
All meter installations under Tranche C must be completed on or before 31 May 2027.
analysis: Why it matters: The order sets procurement, pricing and reporting rules for public metering funds, and requires all supply and installation contracts to be filed with the Commission, which supports transparency over how DisCos spend the money.

also.text: Former NNPC Limited chief Mele Kyari has appeared before a Senate committee, according to a Punch Newspapers report.
The House of Representatives urged NNPC Ltd to convert the Petroleum Industry Act 2021 reforms into higher oil production, investment, refining capacity and tangible benefits for Nigerians.
Access Holdings is reportedly considering an exit from a foreign subsidiary to comply with a Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) rule.
Nigerian-founded fintech Raenest has acquired a 100% ownership stake in Remitise, a UK-based payments company registered with the Financial Conduct Authority.
An opinion-style piece in The Guardian Nigeria News calls for reform of contract awards for the Mambilla hydroelectric project.
A Nigerian court has set aside a forfeiture order against a former managing director of the Warri refinery.
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is digitalising fiscal data collection across Nigeria's 36 states, the Federal Capital Territory and 774 Local Government Areas.
The Nigeria Customs Service has handed over an intercepted consignment of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).
Nigerian insurers' low underwriting capacity and reliance on offshore cover are reported to cost the aviation and maritime sectors about N500 billion yearly.
Enugu State authorities sealed four private hospitals operating illegally and warned against unsafe medical practices.
